title.narrative: Decent Work mainstreamed in the National Development Strategies and other labour related strategies and policies

description.narrative: Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States for the realization of a safe and healthy working environment The Ministry of Labour of the Republic of Djibouti requested ILO's support to put in place an effective and efficient system for preventing occupational risks so as to reduce the number of accidents at work and occupational diseases and to guarantee a state of physical, mental and social well-being in accordance to international standards. The approach agreed is based on the strategic approach proposed by the ILS n°187 on the promotional framework on OSH: systemic approach, tripartism, social dialogue around OSH issues. The approach for the biennium will consist of establishing the national OSH policy, developing adapted OSH programs and strengthen the capacities of labour inspectors in terms of monitoring occupational safety and health conditions. Output A.1. More and better statistics with reliable labour market information systems A comprehensive assessment of the current state of the labour market information system, including international labour migration has been conducted in Djibouti. The assessment underlined that Djibouti’s LMIS is in its infancy, and its development is critical to meet the demands of evidence-based policymaking. Thus, INSTAD requested ILO to provide technical support to assist Djibouti in the design and implementation of their first LFS ensuring the alignment to the latest standards. The LFS will serve as the primary tool to provide the core indicators needed for the LMIS. The approach to improving the knowledgebase of the labour market is to support activities that enhance the national capacity of institutions responsible for legal and statistical indicators. The activities outlined in this CPO will be carried out in collaboration with LMIS Specialists, regional Labour statistician from ROAF, Employment specialist from DWT Cairo, and STAT/Geneva.
